2e24871ec069cd29d238357b5fc247d1bac99e8e: Frabosa Soprana offers 105 km of clearly marked runs — a medium-sized ski area ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 24 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Frabosa Soprana's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Southern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Frabosa Soprana's altitude (891 m at the base, 2085 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in the depths of winter. January and February are the most reliable months; in December and March, it is best to check the conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay at Frabosa Soprana is clearly high: €52 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but it is worth being aware of it before you go. In short: Frabosa Soprana lives up to its promises. A resort in the Southern Alps that will suit most skiers without disappointing.

People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialised skiing of some large ski areas. Ebenalp's modest altitude — starting at 848 m, topping out at 1720 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover.
